learnings.question: Roughly what percentage of newly learned information does a person forget within 24 hours, according to 19th-century psychologist Hermann Ebbinghaus, unless they actively work to recall it?
learnings.learning: Hermann Ebbinghaus, in the 1880s, found that people forget about 80% of what they learn within 24 hours unless they actively force themselves to recall it — which is why spaced repetition (not just re-reading) is needed to retain information.
learnings.articleTitle: Is Your Brain the Worst Place to Store Ideas? Why I Built a Second One

learnings.question: According to a hadith found in Sahih Muslim, a person's good deeds stop being credited to them after death — except for three things. Which of these is NOT one of the three exceptions?
options: A righteous child who prays for them
learnings.learning: The Prophet Muhammad (ﷺ) said that when a person dies, all their deeds end except for three: ongoing charity, beneficial knowledge, or a righteous child who prays for them (Sahih Muslim 1631).
learnings.articleTitle: Is Your Brain the Worst Place to Store Ideas? Why I Built a Second One

learnings.question: In the Scrum agile framework, which artifact is a visual chart used to show the remaining work in a sprint and track whether the team is on schedule?
learnings.learning: The Burndown Chart is a Scrum artifact that visualizes the progress of a Sprint, showing remaining work and helping the team track if they're on schedule.

learnings.question: What is the primary purpose of breaking a software development process into short, iterative cycles known as 'Sprints' in the Scrum framework?
options: To eliminate the need for a project plan
To increase the overall length of the project
To allow for more flexibility and quicker adjustments
To reduce the number of team members needed
learnings.learning: Scrum is an agile approach that breaks the development process into smaller, iterative cycles called Sprints, allowing for more flexibility and quicker adjustments.

learnings.question: In Islamic theology, what Arabic term refers to humanity's role as a steward or caretaker of the Earth?
learnings.learning: Khalifah refers to the Islamic concept of humans serving as caretakers or stewards of the Earth, a role that includes preserving faith and fostering unity within the community.

learnings.question: According to this exploration of life's purpose in Islam, human existence revolves around three primary roles: worshiping Allah, serving as stewards of the Earth, and which third role?
options: Preparing for the eternal Hereafter through a life of conscious choices and accountability
Establishing political authority over other nations
Accumulating wealth to support the community
learnings.learning: Life's purpose in Islam is described as revolving around three primary roles: worshiping Allah, serving as stewards (khalifah) of the Earth, and preparing for the eternal Hereafter through conscious choices and accountability.

learnings.question: Which Quranic teaching emphasizes that in Allah's justice, every deed — no matter how small — is accounted for?
options: Allah does not burden a soul beyond what it can bear
The believers are but brothers to one another
Whoever does an atom's weight of good will see it, and whoever does an atom's weight of evil will see it
learnings.learning: Quran 99:7-8 teaches that in Allah's divine justice, every deed is accounted for no matter how small: whoever does an atom's weight of good will see it, and whoever does an atom's weight of evil will see it.

learnings.question: In PCIe power management, which low-power link state is designed for very short periods of idleness and allows the link to 'wake up' almost instantly to resume full activity?
learnings.learning: L0s is a very light sleep state in PCIe power management, designed for very short durations of idleness, where the link can quickly wake up to resume activity.
learnings.articleTitle: Power Management States in the context of PCIe

learnings.question: Which PCIe power management state is comparable to a computer being completely shut down — offering the greatest power savings but requiring the longest time to resume activity?
learnings.learning: L2 is the deepest PCIe power state, where the device is almost completely powered down — used for the longest periods of inactivity, with the highest power savings and the longest wake-up time.
learnings.articleTitle: Power Management States in the context of PCIe

learnings.question: In Islamic theology, which term refers to the actual, unfolding occurrence of events in a person's life — as opposed to Allah's eternal, preordained knowledge of them?
learnings.learning: Qada' refers to the actual occurrence of events in our lives — the unfolding of events as they happen, shaped by our actions and decisions — while Qadr is Allah's complete, eternal knowledge and plan for everything.
learnings.articleTitle: The Art of Qada’ and Qadr

learnings.question: Which verse from Surah Ar-Ra'd is cited to show that people bear responsibility for changing their own circumstances through action?
options: Indeed, Allah does not change the condition of a people until they change what is in themselves
And whoever fears Allah, He will make for him a way out
So remember Me; I will remember you
learnings.learning: Surah Ar-Ra'd 13:11 states that 'Allah does not change the condition of a people until they change what is in themselves,' underscoring personal responsibility for changing one's own circumstances.
learnings.articleTitle: The Art of Qada’ and Qadr

learnings.question: In an article explaining Qada' and Qadr, what real-life example is used to illustrate how sincere Dua (supplication) can be connected to a change in one's circumstances?
options: A student passing a difficult exam after fasting
A struggling food business turning around and thriving after sincere Dua
A patient recovering from illness after visiting a doctor
A family finding a new home after moving cities
learnings.learning: The article illustrates Qada' being altered through Dua with the example of a struggling food business that begins to thrive after sincere supplication to Allah.
learnings.articleTitle: The Art of Qada’ and Qadr

learnings.question: What data-analysis question motivated an investigation into the most frequently repeated words in the Quran?
options: Whether Quranic verse length correlates with word frequency
Whether translated English words could fully replace the original Arabic vocabulary
Whether digitized Quran texts contain transcription errors
Whether the top 20 most frequent words, following the Pareto Principle, make up roughly 80% of the Quran's text
learnings.learning: The analysis was motivated by the Pareto Principle (80/20 rule): investigating whether the top 20 most frequently used words in the Quran account for roughly 80% of its text.
learnings.articleTitle: Top 20 Words to Understand the Quran: A Data Analysis using Python

learnings.question: In a Pareto-principle-inspired word-frequency analysis of the Quran, what percentage of the Quran's total text did the top 20 most frequently used words actually account for?
learnings.learning: Contrary to the Pareto Principle's 80/20 expectation, the top 20 most frequent words in the Quran accumulate to only about 20.83% of the text.
learnings.articleTitle: Top 20 Words to Understand the Quran: A Data Analysis using Python

learnings.question: What is the term for the small diacritical marks placed above or below Arabic letters to indicate vowel sounds and pronunciation?
learnings.learning: Tashkeel are small markings placed above or below Arabic letters to indicate vowel sounds, similar to how vowels work in English — without them, reading Arabic pronunciation correctly is much harder.
learnings.articleTitle: Top 20 Words to Understand the Quran: A Data Analysis using Python
